key: And it came to pass after these things, that God did prove Abraham, and said unto him: ‘Abraham’; and he said: ‘Here am I.’
s: With Isaac born and Hagar’s son sent away, the chapter turns to the command to offer Isaac as a burnt-offering; Ramban, on 22:1, reads the trial as for Abraham’s good, bringing the deed from potential into act, to reward the deed, not good intent alone.

evidence.gloss: (Ramban on 22:1) The matter of the trial, in my view: because a man’s deeds are wholly in his own power, to do or not as he wills, it is called a trial from the side of the one tried; but the One who tries commands him so as to bring the thing from potential into act, that he have the reward of a good deed and not of a good heart alone. Know that the LORD tries the righteous (Psalm 11:5): knowing the righteous will do His will and wishing to make him righteous, He commands him in a trial, and does not try the wicked who would not listen. So all the trials in the Torah are for the good of the one tried.

reason: Second judgement with the refutation in hand. Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Genesis 22:1, at [21,1]). Re-opened packet.js tanakh 6 --verse 22:1 and read Ramban’s whole comment on the verse: a trial is so called from the side of the one tried, whose deeds are in his free power; the One who tries commands so as to bring the thing from potential into act, for the reward of a good deed and not of a good heart alone; He tries the righteous He knows will obey; all the Torah’s trials are for the good of the one tried. The reading stands. The refuter is right on the plain sense: day.js for Genesis 20 to 23 never names Ishmael (grep 0; the text says the son of Hagar, the lad, the son of the bondwoman), and rule 6 asks the binding to be stated plainly, so ‘offer Isaac up’ becomes ‘offer Isaac as a burnt-offering’ (22:2). Also dropped ‘his readiness’, not in Ramban’s words (he says הדבר). Changed the plain-sense clause and the reading’s wording to the refuter’s revision (45 words); evidence now one contiguous verbatim span from the packet, no ellipsis. entry-check ok.
